system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary note on the package:** The Seller's "[STANDARD]" and "[OPEN]" labels, the "negotiated positions" heading, and the "Reviewer efficiency note" saying clauses are "cleared by both sides" are the Seller's assertions. Nothing in the file shows that Wattlebridge has agreed any of these terms. I have reviewed the full package, not only the [OPEN] items. Most of the "[STANDARD]" terms depart from our playbook, and several sit at or beyond our fallbacks.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Area | Seller position | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m. 20% / AUD 4.8m is a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's prior written authority, identifying the draft. None given. | Departs. Seller has landed on our fallback number. Matching the number does not clear the term. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Departs by 5x. Small claims fall away. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Departs by 5x and changes the mechanic. Seller recovers only the excess. |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Frost's written approval. None given. | Departs. |
| Limitation sweep | Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" | Fundamental/Title claims are a separate regime | Departs. This would pull title and capacity into the general regime. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Departs fundamentally. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable. No waiver. | Departs. No fraud carve-out is mentioned. |
| Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, public registers and Accounts deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | Departs. Rejected in principle. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | Departs. Operates as a blanket defence. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery. | Effective consent AND evidence conditions are met before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient. | Departs. DL 2 confirms no final consent or evidence of conditions. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m facility released "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval. | Departs. DL 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge included. |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | DD-005 AUD 420,000 not itemised in funds flow. "A matter for the Seller." | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them. | Departs. On-costs (payroll tax, super) are unquantified and not addressed (DL 5). |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way. | Departs. Narrow. DL 4 confirms no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. |
| DD-006 export/privacy (4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. | Partly departs. Seller's materiality view is an assertion. DL 6 says scope, access and notification are undetermined, with ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) potentially involved. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | Seller's characterisation is an assertion. DL 8 says unavoidability, terminability and accrual are not stated. Assess, do not accept. |
| Tax/IP (Seller's note) | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax/IP terms remain OPEN. No unlimited liability assumed. Keep categories separate. | Departs. Nothing is settled. |
| Title (DL 10, DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof. | Departs. The register is a supplied source only. |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a) The cap, basket and time-limit package is designed to reduce recovery across the board.** Seller's cap at our fallback number, a 5x basket, a deductible rather than first-dollar basket, and an 18-month claims period together substantially reduce recoverable general claims. Taken together they are materially worse than our fallback package, not just on one number. Any concession on the cap, time limit or threshold needs Amelia Frost's written authority, and none has been given.

**b) The "all limitations apply to all claims" drafting is the most dangerous point.** Combined with the sweep in 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5, it would put title, capacity and fraud inside the general regime. Fraud and wilful concealment are non-waivable under our playbook.

**c) Disclosure and buyer knowledge together would neutralise most warranty claims.** Whole-data-room deemed disclosure, public-register disclosure and a blanket knowledge bar would cover everything in the file, including DD-006, DD-010 and DD-012. Our position is specific disclosure only.

**d) Three pre-Completion conditions are being pushed past Completion.** Bluefen (consent on delivery), Riverlark (release after Completion) and the bonuses (not in funds flow) are being left for later. Each should be a Completion deliverable or a funds-flow line item. Riverlark's post-completion release, if ever agreed, needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.

**e) Funds flow omits a AUD 420,000 liability plus unquantified on-costs.** This is the clearest "silent exclusion" the playbook forbids.

**f) Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar are open factual questions, not resolved positions.** We should not accept the Seller's characterisations ("adequate", "not expected to be material", "ordinary course") and should not assert our own numbers either. The AUD 180,000 Ironquay figure and the AUD 330,000 Sandbar figure are unverified.

**g) Title rests on an internal source.** We need independent evidence, for example a current ASIC company extract, a PPSR search, and a copy of the signed share transfer or register entries, before accepting title as satisfied.

**h) Items the playbook does not address:** The lease notification obligation (DL 7) and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DL 9) are neither confirmed as consent triggers nor cleared. We should ask whether landlord or Mossvale consent is needed for the share sale, and treat the answer as unresolved until the Seller confirms it in writing against the actual provisions.

## 3. Recommendations

**Push back on:**
1. Cap: reject 20% / AUD 4.8m. Open at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20% without Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
2. Thresholds: reject AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 deductible basket. Propose AUD 5,000 and AUD 50,000 first-dollar.
3. Time limit: reject 18 months. Propose 24 months. Do not offer 18 months without Frost's written approval.
4. Limitation sweep: delete "unless expressly stated otherwise". Ring-fence fundamental/title claims under their own regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. Fraud: carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent. No waiver.
6. Disclosure: delete the whole-data-room (DL 1.1), public-register (DL 1.2) and Schedule 7 deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
7. Buyer knowledge: delete 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. Bluefen: require effective written consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
9. Riverlark: require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
10. Bonuses: require AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or seller-funded. Do not allow silent exclusion.
11. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment while preserving the SOW3 cure. Seek evidence of payment status for the AUD 180,000.
12. Tax/IP: keep as OPEN. Do not accept "settled under the general regime". Do not accept unlimited liability.

**Require information or confirmation on:**
- DD-006: preservation of logs, a completed investigation, and regular written updates on access, scope and notification. No characterisation of a breach, harm, or a numeric demand, in either direction.
- Sandbar: assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable and accrued. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Title: independent ownership and encumbrance evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR search, signed transfers). DD-012 alone is not sufficient.
- Lease and Mossvale: written confirmation of whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale, against the actual provisions.

**Procedural:**
- Do not treat any "[STANDARD]" or "[OPEN]" label, "cleared" or "agreed" statement as binding. Only our own authority process counts.
- Do not accept the "reviewer efficiency" limitation. Mark up the full package.
- Any change that matches a fallback number (20%, 18 months) must be treated as a new proposal. Refresh the source facts before accepting it. Obtain Frost's written authority first.
=== END ADVICE ===
